3. At the trial both the parties adduced oral as well as documentary evidence to prove their respective cases. 

 4. The suit was transferred to the Assistant Judge, Ramgati, Lakshmipur vide Miscellaneous Order No.67 of the learned District Judge, Lakshmipur dated 25.11.1993. 

 9. Mr. Abul Hossain Azadi, the learned Advocate argued that though the trial court set aside the judgment and decree dated 10.04.1984 in Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 but it is found that no order of restoration of the suit in its original file and number and when an ex-parte decree is set-aside then the original suit must be restored to its original file and number relying upon the decision reported in 43 DLR (HCD)- 48. He further argued that since both the Courts set-aside the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 in such a case his only submission is that the said suit must be restored to its original file and number for disposal of the same afresh. 

 10. Mr. Muhammad Salahuddin, the learned Advocate has also conceded the said argument of the learned Advocate of the petitioner. He argued that as per decision of the case reported in 43 DLR (HCD)-48 the Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 may be restored to its original file and number for disposal of the same afresh but the Rule may be discharged. 

 11. I have considered the case of Gulshan Ara Begum alias Jahanara and others -versus- Moazzem Hossain and others reported in 43 DLR(HCD)-48 wherein their Lordship held: 

 "In that view of the matter we hold. that the summons were not duly served upon the petitioners in accordance with law and the learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law in his decision resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No.61 of 1987 and rejecting the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the above circumstances we feel that ends of justice will he met, if we set aside the ex-parte decree dated 29.10.1987 and restore the original suit to its file and number." 

 13. On perusal of the record it is found that the ex-parte decree dated 10.04.1984 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Lakshmipur in Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 but it appears that the said judgment and decree was set-aside by the Assistant Judge. In normal course the Assistant Judge has no authority to interfere with the judgment and decree passed by the superior court i.e. the Subordinate Judge. It appears that by Miscellaneous Order No.67 dated 25.11.1993 of the learned District Judge the suit was transferred to the Senior Assistant Judge. It also appears that the opposite parties filed the said suit before the Subordinate Judge and perhaps when the pecuniary jurisdiction has been increased then the said matter may be sent to the Court of Assistant Judge by the learned District Judge. Though it is not the disputed question in the instant case, but since it is found that the Assistant Judge interfere with the judgment of the superior court i.e. the Subordinate Judge, so, it should be considered whether the inferior Court can hear the said matter. It appears that perhaps firstly, may be for increasing the pecuniary jurisdiction the trial court has empowered to hear the aforesaid suit, since it appears that the learned District Judge vide administrative order No.67 dated 25.11.1993 transferred the said suit to the Assistant Judge. Secondly, if any fraud committed in obtaining any decree or order in any case then the Assistant Judge can consider the matter though earlier decree or order passed by the superior Court. 

 14. Mr. Salahuddin, the learned Advocate argued that the fraud vitiates everything and since without any summons the plaintiffs of the earlier suit i.e. the present petitioners obtained ex-parte decree in Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 in such a case the Assistant Judge, can interfere with the said matter. He further argued that the present opposite- parties rightly filed the case before the Subordinate Judge when the said Court had pecuniary jurisdiction but when the pecuniary jurisdiction having been increased, the learned District Judge by its administrative order sent the suit to the Assistant Judge for hearing. It appears that the trial Court found that the said ex-parte decree obtained by committing fraud and without any summons in such a case the Assistant Judge is empowered to set aside the ex-parte decree passed by the superior Court. 

 15. The case of Sarthakram Maiti-versus-Nundo Ram Maiti reported in 11 The Calcutta Weekly Notes-579, where a Division Bench of Calcutta High Court after consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case has taken view that if fraud has been committed in obtaining any decree then the Assistant Judge can consider the judgment of the superior Court. Their Lordship held: 

 "The only point raised in support of this appeal is that the Munsif had no jurisdiction under the law to declare a decree to be a nullity which had been passed by a court of superior jurisdiction namely, the court of the Subordinate Judge. In support of the contention, reliance has been placed on the cases of Aushootosh Chandra --v- Tara Prosanna Roy (1) and Kedar Nath Mukharjee -v- Prosonna Kumar Chatterjee (2) We do not, however, find that in either of the decisions in these two cases it has been laid down that a court of inferior jurisdiction is incompetent, when otherwise it has jurisdiction in dealing with a suit, to declare a judgment to be a nullity when that judgment has been given in a court of superior jurisdiction and when it is proved that it is vitiated by reason of fraud. There can be no doubt, on the authorities quoted, that fraud invalidates all proceedings obtained there by; and though a Court of inferior jurisdiction may not have the power to set aside a decree passed by a court of superior jurisdiction, on the grounds it has been obtained by fraud, still it has, in our opinion, the power at least to treat it as a nullity and to pass a judgment declaring it to be so. This is the view taken in the case of Nunda Lal Bose —v-Nistarini Dasses (3) on which the Munsif has relied. We can find no authority in the case to which we have referred for holding that in this case the Munsif had no jurisdiction. The value of the decree which was obtained by fraud was Rs.607-1 1-3 and a suit brought in respect of that sum, would, certainly, under the provisions of law, be one which must be instituted in the Munsif's court as the court of the lowest pecuniary jurisdiction competent to try it. We, therefore, see no grounds for differing from the view taken by the lower court in this case and we dismiss the appeal with costs." 

 16. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the discussions made above. The Rule is discharged with modification of the order. The impugned judgment and decree dated 30.08.2001 passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Lakshmipur in Title Appeal No.42 of 2005 affirming those dated 26.09.1995 passed by the Assistant Judge, Ramgati, Lakshmipur in Other Class Suit No.250 of 1993 are hereby upheld subject to restore the Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 to its original file and number. 

 17. Since Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 is a long pending case the trial court is directed to dispose of the suit as early as possible preferably within 6 months from the date of receipt of this judgment in accordance with law.
